name: veterinary_clinic_system_037_vaccine_stock_shrink
instruction: A stock-shrink audit found that every vaccine SKU in pharmacy_inventory was overcounted, and the shrink must be reconciled against real upcoming demand. The shrink percentage for THIS episode is stored in veterinary_clinic_system_ops_meta.shrink_pct as an integer percent. (1) For every pharmacy_inventory row whose item_name contains 'vaccine' (case-sensitive substring), reduce quantity_on_hand by shrink_pct percent and round DOWN to a whole number of units — new quantity = floor(old_quantity * (100 - shrink_pct) / 100) — and on each row you change also set shrink_adjusted = the episode batch_code and pre_shrink_qty = the quantity_on_hand the row held before this episode's shrink. No other inventory row may change. (2) For every vaccine_type present in the vaccinations collection, push one ops_reports row with report='vaccine_shrink', batch_code, vaccine_type, pre_doses = the total on-hand units for that vaccine across all locations before the shrink (the sum of pre_shrink_qty over that type's rows), post_doses = the same after the shrink, demand_next_30 = the count of vaccinations rows of that vaccine_type whose due_date falls in the inclusive window [episode_date, episode_date + 30 days], and coverage_status = 'adequate' if post_doses >= demand_next_30 else 'short'. To match a vaccine inventory row to its vaccine_type, take the leading word of item_name and match it case-insensitively to vaccinations.vaccine_type (e.g. 'Bordetella vaccine' -> 'bordetella', 'DHPP vaccine' -> 'DHPP'). (3) Append one audit_log row: actor='system', actor_role='system', action='VACCINE_SHRINK_AUDIT', target_collection='pharmacy_inventory', target_id='bulk', batch_code, details='Vaccine shrink <batch_code>: <shrink_pct>% applied to <N> vaccine SKUs' where N is the number of inventory rows you adjusted, occurred_at = the episode timestamp. No other collection may change, and non-vaccine inventory rows (including controlled-substance items) must remain byte-identical.
_steps_note: par_steps and max_steps must be measured from a real gold.py run against a live container in the QC session (RL_ENV_HARDMODE_CODEGEN_PROMPT); intentionally null here — do not guess a round number.

success_criteria.summary: Every pharmacy_inventory row whose item_name contains 'vaccine' (8 seeded rows: ids 1-8) has quantity_on_hand = floor(seed_qty*(100-shrink_pct)/100), shrink_adjusted == batch_code, and pre_shrink_qty == the seeded quantity_on_hand; all other inventory rows byte-identical. ops_reports holds exactly one vaccine_shrink row per vaccine_type for this batch with pre_doses recomputed from the snapshot, post_doses recomputed from live post-shrink inventory, demand_next_30 recomputed two independent ways (raw-row Python filter vs SQL COUNT with a BETWEEN window) which must agree, and coverage_status derived from post_doses >= demand_next_30. audit_log gains exactly one VACCINE_SHRINK_AUDIT row. All seeded collections outside the blast radius are canary-checked byte-identical.

checks.expect: 8 vaccine rows floor-shrunk + tagged; other 34 rows byte-identical
demand_next_30 per type agrees between a raw-row Python due_date filter and an independent SQL COUNT(*) ... BETWEEN
exactly len(vaccine_types) vaccine_shrink rows for batch_code; every field asserted incl. coverage_status
seed count + 1; new VACCINE_SHRINK_AUDIT row exact incl. batch_code

hazards: Only 8 of the 42 pharmacy_inventory rows are vaccines (ids 1-8: 'Rabies vaccine 1yr', 'DHPP vaccine', 'FVRCP vaccine', 'Bordetella vaccine' at locations 1 and 2). The selection is a case-sensitive substring on item_name, not category='medication' — the 34 non-vaccine rows include 10 non-vaccine medication rows (ids 9-18), 16 supply rows (ids 19-34), and 8 controlled-substance rows (ids 35-42) that must stay byte-identical.

shrink_pct is an integer percent (5-20) in ops_meta, not a fraction: an agent that multiplies by (1 - shrink_pct) shrinks stock by 95-80x instead of 5-20%, and one that rounds instead of flooring fails on rows like Bordetella (9 units: 15% -> floor(7.65)=7, not 8).

vaccine_type matching is case-sensitive in the data: vaccinations.vaccine_type values are 'rabies', 'DHPP', 'FVRCP', 'bordetella' while item_names are 'Rabies vaccine 1yr', 'DHPP vaccine', 'FVRCP vaccine', 'Bordetella vaccine' — a case-sensitive or whole-name match silently drops two of the four types.

demand_next_30 is an inclusive [episode_date, episode_date+30] window over ~600 vaccinations rows, and episode_date itself jitters per episode — at ep=2026-09-30 the per-type counts are rabies 12, DHPP 10, FVRCP 9, bordetella 7, so an off-by-one boundary produces a plausible-but-wrong coverage_status on borderline types.

Idempotency is checked: a naive re-run re-applies the shrink to already-shrunk rows (second pass would take Rabies 30 -> 27 at 10% instead of staying 30) — the verifier derives expected quantities from the snapshot, not from live state, so double-shrinking fails. Equally, leaving shrink_adjusted/pre_shrink_qty unset or set to stale values fails — the verifier checks pre_shrink_qty equals the seeded quantity exactly.

Bordetella vaccine (ids 7-8, quantity_on_hand 9, reorder_level 10) is already at/below reorder before the shrink — an agent that skips already-low rows 'because they need reordering not shrinking' leaves unshrunk rows and fails the exact-quantity check. Likewise ops_reports is absent from the seed snapshot (not one of the 24 seeded collections) and audit_log's 4 seeded rows include a CS_LOG_APPENDED decoy (id 3) that must not be edited — the run must create the report rows blind and append exactly one audit row.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Extends v1's flat shrink pass into a shrink-and-reconcile mission: the randomized percent (ops_meta) is applied to live inventory AND the resulting stock is scored against real vaccination demand in a 30-day window, reported per vaccine_type with an adequacy flag, and closed with an audit entry. Case-insensitive type matching, floor rounding, the inclusive date window, and rerun-safe tagging are where plausible-but-wrong solutions fail.
